title: When the Inventory Turns
premise: Felix Kavanagh, once a violin prodigy whose career ended in an unexplained scandal at twenty-two, returns to the Aldergate Conservatory as a night janitor, hiding in plain sight among the corridors he once owned. When the auction of his late teacher's estate surfaces an old letter implicating Felix's best friend in the sabotage that destroyed them both, Felix must choose between the loyalty that has defined his silence and a truth that could restore his name. As the conservatory prepares to demolish the rehearsal hall where everything went wrong, Felix confronts his friend, now its celebrated director, and finally speaks the accusation he has rehearsed for two decades. The book ends not with vindication but with testimony: Felix plays the hall's last concert on a borrowed violin, tells the story aloud, and walks out unnamed but no longer invisible.
about_author: Isandro Ishikawa is the pen name of a former orchestral librarian who spent fifteen years cataloguing other people's music before turning to fiction. Raised between Kyoto and Cork, they write about institutions, memory, and the people who sweep the floors of great buildings.

chapters.title: The Man Who Mops the Stage
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Introduces his nightly rounds at the conservatory, the ritual of avoiding the rehearsal hall, and the small kindnesses that keep him anonymous. A student recognizes his hands' posture at a piano and asks if he plays; he says he used to. Emotional beat: the ache of chosen erasure.

chapters.title: Estate Sale, Lot 44
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. He learns his late teacher Marta Ilves's house and belongings are going to auction and attends the preview incognito. Among the sheet music he finds a sealed letter addressed to him, dated the week of the scandal. He leaves without opening it. Emotional beat: dread dressed as curiosity.

chapters.title: Almost Saying It
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with a flashback to age twelve. We see young Felix and his best friend Tobias rehearsing a duo in the old hall, and the first hint of the rivalry Marta cultivated between them. Felix opens the letter at home and stops halfway. Emotional beat: the past pressing through the floorboards.

chapters.title: What the Letter Didn't Finish
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The letter's surviving fragment suggests Marta knew the truth about the sabotaged audition and meant to confess. Felix begins quietly investigating the auction lots, tracking down the estate's executor. Emotional beat: the first crack in twenty years of discipline.

chapters.title: The Director's Corridor
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. Tobias, now conservatory director, announces the rehearsal hall's demolition and a farewell gala. He is charismatic, exhausted, and haunted in ways he won't name. He passes Felix in the corridor without recognition—or without showing it. Emotional beat: two men orbiting the same wound.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Working nights, Felix catalogs the hall's contents before demolition and finds Marta's old annotation ledger hidden in a piano bench. Its entries stop abruptly on the date of the scandal. Emotional beat: evidence as a kind of haunting.

chapters.title: The Prodigy Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Alternating flashback, Felix's POV. The full story of the audition day: the broken E-string, the accusation of tampering, Felix's refusal to defend himself, and Tobias's silent complicity in the narrative that Felix did it to him. Emotional beat: the machinery of a lie assembling itself.

chapters.title: A Buyer for Everything
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At the auction, Felix bids recklessly on a case of Marta's correspondence and wins it with money he doesn't have, borrowing from a fellow janitor, Dee, who demands to know why. He lies; she doesn't believe him. Emotional beat: the cost of secrets compounding.

chapters.title: Correspondence
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The letters reveal Marta's decades of guilt and her suspicion that Tobias's father, a board member, orchestrated the sabotage to protect Tobias's career. Felix's hands shake reading it. Emotional beat: grief for a teacher who chose silence too.

chapters.title: Dee's Question
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. Dee, a former legal aid lawyer turned custodian, researches Felix's name and finds the old scandal coverage. Instead of confronting him, she leaves the printout on his cart with one word: 'Talk.' Emotional beat: loyalty offered before it is earned.

chapters.title: The Gala Committee
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. Planning the farewell gala, Tobias discovers the annotation ledger is missing from the inventory and suspects a thief. His paranoia curdles into something older. He requests the hall's security footage. Emotional beat: guilt wearing the mask of authority.

chapters.title: Practice Room 7
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix breaks into the hall at night and, alone, plays for the first time in twenty years—badly, then less badly. The footage catches him. He knows it. Emotional beat: the body remembering what the life denied.

chapters.title: Footage
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. Tobias watches the tape and recognizes Felix's hands before his face. Instead of reporting him, he summons Felix to his office and offers him a place in the gala program—'the janitor who plays,' a charming human-interest spot. Emotional beat: an olive branch that is also a muzzle.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In Tobias's office, the two men dance around the past; Tobias offers redemption-as-novelty, and Felix realizes Tobias still believes, or needs to believe, Felix was the saboteur. Felix accepts the slot, intending to use the stage. Emotional beat: a bargain made in bad faith by both.

chapters.title: The Executor's Testimony
chapters.summary: Felix and Dee's POV, alternating. They track down Marta's executor, who reveals Marta spent her final years trying to get the conservatory to reopen the case and was quietly blocked by the board—Tobias's father's old allies. Emotional beat: justice revealed as something deferred, not denied.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix confronts the wreckage of the choice ahead: exposing Tobias could destroy the conservatory, the students, the hall's legacy—everything Marta built. Dee challenges him: whose comfort is his silence protecting? Emotional beat: the theme made explicit and refused as an excuse.

chapters.title: Tobias, Alone
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. The night before the gala, Tobias visits the empty hall and remembers the truth he has never said aloud: he saw his father tamper with Felix's instrument and chose his inheritance over his friend. He drafts a resignation letter he doesn't send. Emotional beat: confession rehearsed, again, in private.

chapters.title: The Last Concert
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The farewell gala. Felix performs on Marta's restored violin before a full house, playing the duo he and Tobias once played together. Mid-piece, he stops, and tells the hall the story—the sabotage, the silence, the name that was never his to carry. Emotional beat: the climax; the art of almost saying it, ended.

chapters.title: Aftermath, First Movement
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The hall erupts—not in scandal but in stunned recognition; students demand answers, the board scrambles, and Tobias walks onstage and confirms Felix's account, then resigns from the podium, not the institution. Emotional beat: truth landing without triumph.

chapters.title: What the Demolition Spares
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The hall is demolished anyway, but the conservatory establishes the Ilves Fellowship and invites Felix to teach—not as a prodigy restored, but as a witness. He declines the title 'maestro' and accepts the work. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt on terms he chooses.

chapters.title: Two Chairs
chapters.summary: Felix and Tobias's POV, alternating. Months later, the two men meet in a practice room—not forgiven, not friends, but playing the old duo again, badly, honestly. Tobias asks why Felix came back as a janitor; Felix says he wanted to hear the building without an audience. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth reconciled, imperfectly.

chapters.title: When the Inventory Turns
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, final. Felix leads his first seminar in the new building, teaching students to listen for what isn't played. He keeps Marta's ledger on his desk, its last blank page finally filled with his own account, signed with his full name. Emotional beat: resolution—visibility chosen, silence ended, justice carried rather than won.
